Project VektaKillzone HD: Unofficial PC Port (static recompilation)

A native Linux and Windows x64 port of the 2011 PS3 remaster of the first Killzone, made by static recompilation: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C++ ahead of time and compiled into a PC program on your machine; graphics go through Vulkan. No emulator runs at play time.

Status: Playable

You need your own copy of the game. This project ships no game code, data, assets or keys.

See the statusSource on GitHub

Every feature, with evidence >

Unreleased

not released yet

  • ChangedThe music and the other MP3 streams are decoded by the port itself (minimp3, CC0), in place of the PS3 system software's MP3 decoder, which ran translated. Compared with it in Levels 1 and 4: the same frames, the same silences, samples within 50 dB SNR. KZ_MP3_PIC=1 runs the firmware's decoder instead. The firmware's flashMP3.pic is still read when the game starts its sound.
  • ChangedThe firmware's libsre.prx is no longer needed: the SPURS queue the game sends its compressed data requests through, which ran the firmware's own libsre code, is now in the port's runtime (ps3recomp patch 1022, checked against libsre on 46,000 random cases; after Project Pyrrhus patch 6003, MIT). The installers stop asking for it, and on the RPCS3 route your RPCS3 decrypts only the game's EBOOT. PS3 system software 4.93 is still needed for the music (its dev_flash, read as installed). The lift no longer makes work/fw, and removes the one an earlier version made.

0.5.3

19 Nov 2026 · pre-release

  • FixedThe PlayStation Store copy of Killzone HD (NPUA80856) installs. Its data_ps3.psarc.edat is bound to the buyer's licence, which the port cannot open, so the first-run check stopped on it with "DIFFERENT" (#67). "Use my RPCS3 install" now has your RPCS3 decrypt a copy of it too, with the licence (.rap) it already uses for the game, into work/prep/data_ps3.psarc: the same archive as the disc copy's, checked by its SHA-256. Without RPCS3, the check names the Store copy and says to use that route.
  • FixedChoosing Quit Game in the first seconds (as from the main menu right after the start) no longer shows "The game stopped right after it started": the launcher now takes the game's own quit line as the player's choice.
  • Changed"Use my RPCS3 install" names, on the setup's build page, each file your RPCS3 is decrypting, and links instead of copying the game's files it decrypts when they are on the same drive as the port (no second 3 GB copy).

0.5.2

18 Nov 2026 · pre-release

  • AddedFinding RPCS3 by hand: the setup's "Your game" page has a "Find RPCS3..." button, and run.cmd, ./run.sh and tools/install.sh a fourth choice, "My RPCS3 is somewhere else", for an RPCS3 the automatic search did not find. The folder can be where rpcs3.exe is, RPCS3's config folder or the game folder RPCS3 installed; the setup keeps it for the next run (/RPCS3=<dir> gives it on the command line).
  • FixedThe build works in an install folder with a space in its path (as D:\Games\My Games\Project Vekta): the force-included headers and the Windows toolchain's include and library folders are now quoted, where clang stopped with "no such file" on the part of the path after the space.
  • Fixed"Use my RPCS3 install" finds a portable RPCS3 unzipped two folders down a drive or the home folder (as D:\Games\PS3\rpcs3-...), and a path anywhere inside RPCS3 (its dev_hdd0\game\NPUA80856, dev_flash or a file in them, or its game folder where vfs.yml keeps it outside RPCS3) now counts as pointing at that RPCS3.
  • FixedThe first run (run.cmd, ./run.sh, tools/install.sh) offers "Use my RPCS3 install" again after a failed check when the paths came from an earlier install or point into RPCS3, and takes EBOOT.elf, data_ps3.psarc or libsre.prx from a folder given for them. The check now says what a folder given for a file is (the installed game's folder holds only the encrypted EBOOT.BIN and .edat; a folder that is not dev_flash) instead of "nothing at", and how to go on.
  • ChangedThe FFmpeg the Windows and Linux builds download is now served from this repository's own release (deps-ffmpeg-n9.0.2-57-gd838f9f9ae, BtbN's autobuild-2026-11-16-15-29 byte for byte, same SHA-256 pins), with FFmpeg's source for that build beside it, so a removed upstream build can no longer break a release as it did 0.5.0. A new deps-mirror workflow publishes a re-pin (docs/dev/deps-mirror.md).

The whole changelog >

About the port

how it works · ps3recomp v0.19.0 · 156 patches

The port is built on ps3recomp (MIT), pinned at v0.19.0 with 156 patches of this project: the PPU code and the game's SPU programs are lifted to C++, the PS3 system libraries the game calls are reimplemented, and the game's RSX command stream is replayed on Vulkan. It builds natively on Linux, and on Linux for Windows; the Windows build is tested under Wine, Proton and on Windows.

It follows Project Helghast and Project Pyrrhus, the same method applied to Killzone 3 and Killzone 2, and reuses their general runtime work. About 65 % of Killzone HD is done, and 43 % of the whole trilogy plan; what comes next: the roadmap.

Full status

Install

v0.5.3 pre-release

19 Nov 2026 · playable · source for Linux x64

Download v0.5.3All releases

The release page has project-vekta-0.5.3-source.tar.gz (this version's tree with ps3recomp at its pinned commit) with a .sha256 file, and SHA256SUMS: check your download against them. There is no installer yet: the archive builds the port as below.

The build checks your own Killzone HD files, translates the game's code and builds it on your machine. Nothing of the game is shipped or downloaded, and nothing is written into your game files. What each input must contain: Getting your files.

git clone --recurse-submodules \
  https://github.com/gustavomorinaga/project-vekta
cd project-vekta
tools/check-game-files.py
tools/ps3recomp-patched.sh
tools/lift.sh
tools/setup-vfs.sh
tools/build.sh
tools/play.sh

The steps, and the Windows build: building.

What goes online

Nothing. The port, its scripts and the build make no network connection of their own; the only downloads are the ones you start (this repository, its ps3recomp submodule, your system's packages). Where your saves and settings go: the README.

Viewing this website loads the Fira Sans Condensed font from Google Fonts, which sees your visit; the repository, the build and the game do not.

Requirements

What you need

Your own Killzone HD (NPUA80856) from the Killzone Trilogy disc, installed, with its decrypted EBOOT and data archive, and the dev_flash of PS3 system software 4.93 (for the music): GETTING-FILES.md. No PlayStation Network account is used.

Hardware to play

MinimumTested
Operating systemLinux x64; Windows x64 (other Windows versions and machines not tried)CachyOS (Linux x64); the maintainer's Windows install for the cross-built exe; Wine and Proton (GE-Proton 11, proton-cachyos)
CPUx86-64 with AVX2 (x86-64-v3, Intel Haswell or AMD Zen and newer), the default build target; KZ_MARCH="" builds for any x86-64, untestedthe maintainer's desktop CPU with AVX-512 (KZ_MARCH=x86-64-v4)
GPUa Vulkan GPU and driver; NVIDIA DLSS needs an NVIDIA RTX GPU, AMD FSR 3.1 runs on any; a tester's AMD Radeon 8060S on Windows runs it with open problems (KNOWN_ISSUES.md, issues #17 and #18), other GPUs not tried yetNVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti, driver 615
Memorybuilding: several GB for the lifted code (use fewer jobs on small machines); playing: not measured
Diskabout 4 GB for your game files, plus, free: Windows about 2.4 GB (the release folder 0.75 GB, then the build: lifted code 0.13 GB, work\build-win 0.38 GB, work\win-deps 0.20 GB, the game folder work\vfs with the movies taken out of the archive 0.92 GB), and about 3.2 GB more where Windows cannot make links, for copies of the EBOOT and the archive (the setup program reserves 5.8 GB); Linux about 1.9 GB (the folder 0.57 GB, lifted code 0.13 GB, work/build 0.26 GB, work/vfs 0.92 GB; the EBOOT and the archive are linked)measured 2026-11-14 on the maintainer's machine (main at 698c28c), and the v0.4.0 downloads unpacked

Notice and creditsLicence (MIT)Project HelghastProject Pyrrhus

Killzone and Killzone HD are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Guerrilla Games; the names are used only to say which game the port runs. "Vekta" is the name of the game's own colony world. No game content is distributed: no disc or PSN files, no decrypted or translated game code, no assets, no firmware and no keys. Players supply their own copy of the game; the game's code is translated and compiled on the player's own machine from their own files.

The port's own code, tools and documentation are MIT. Third-party components and credits: NOTICE.md. Temporal upscaling: AMD FidelityFX FSR 3.1 (MIT, built in) and NVIDIA DLSS (NVIDIA's, under its own licence; downloaded from NVIDIA on the player's machine only when they accept it, and never distributed here). AMD, FidelityFX, NVIDIA and DLSS are trademarks of their owners.
